[[File:Julio Fernando Navarro Portrait.png|thumb|Portrait of Julio Navarro]]
'''Julio F. Navarro''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Canada|FRSC]] (born October 12, 1962 in [[Santiago del Estero]], [[Argentina]]) is a professor of [[Astronomy]] (Ph.D. [[Universidad Nacional de Córdoba]], Argentina) at the department of Physics and Astronomy in the [[University of Victoria]]. Navarro's research is mainly focused on the formation and evolution of galaxies and galaxy clusters and the structure and evolution of their dark matter component. He is known for his theoretical studies of [[dark matter]] halos carried out using massive N-body simulations.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Julio F. Navarro's research works {{!}} University of Victoria, Victoria (UVIC) and other places|url=https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Julio-F-Navarro-6459399|access-date=2021-02-09|website=ResearchGate|language=en}}</ref> Navarro along with [[Carlos Frenk]] and [[Simon White]] has formulated a density profile for dark matter halos, which was [[NFW profile|named after them]]. In 2015, he won the [[Henry Marshall Tory Medal]] of the [[Royal Society of Canada]]. He is [[Editor-in-chief|chief editor]] of the journal [[Frontiers Media|Frontiers in Astronomy and Space Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/astronomy-and-space-sciences|title=Frontiers in Astronomy and Space Sciences|website=www.frontiersin.org|language=en|access-date=2019-11-13}}</ref>
